title: Decoder: fix signaling and detection of illegal instructions
body:
This commit fixes two bugs in the decoder:

1. For illegal branch condition selections, the illegal instruction
condition must be signaled as long as the instruction is being executed
and not just during the first cycle, as the controller cannot interrupt
multicycle instructions.

2. Illegal instructions should also be signaled when `instr[28]` is set
for register-register ALU operations. Previously, these were not
signaled as the original design used `instr[28]` to encode custom bit-
manipulation instructions.

These bugs were discovered by @taoliug. This resolves issue #163.

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

resolved_issues.title: 7d10b363 is not decoded as illegal instruction
resolved_issues.body:
Based on the RISC-V instruction encoding, 7d10b363 doesn't map to any legal instruction. The trace log shows the instruction as INVALID. However, the id_stage doesn't assert the illegal_insn signal, and the core continues executing the instructions without jump to exception handling routine. Looks like the core can only detect illegal compressed instructions and illegal CSR instructions.

Spike log

```
core   0: 0xffffffff8000faaa (0x7d10b363) unknown
core   0: exception trap_illegal_instruction, epc 0xffffffff8000faaa
core   0:           tval 0x0000000000000000
core   0: 0x000000008001d000 (0x00007119) addi    sp, sp, -128
```

ibex log
```
            22039000           10921 8000faa8 40b6d693 srai             x13, x13, 0x40b     x13=0x00000000 x13:0x00000000
            22041000           10922 8000faaa 7d10b363 INVALID                             
            22047000           10925 8000faae 001d0d13 addi             x26, x26, 1         x26=0x5fab433a x26:0x5fab4339

```

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/ibex
git fetch --all --tags --prune || true
git checkout -f c96ece04296c3c69df578d760aa8a66f9b886fef
git submodule update --init --recursive

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
apt-get update
apt-get install -y verilator g++

cat > /etc/profile.d/ibex-local-path.sh <<'EOF'
export PATH="/usr/bin:$PATH"
EOF

export PATH="/usr/bin:$PATH"
problem_statement: The Ibex decoder fails to classify some register-register ALU instruction encodings as illegal. In this core configuration, a 32-bit register-register ALU instruction with bit 28 set is not a supported instruction, but the decoder can still let it execute and the core then falls through to the next instruction instead of taking an illegal-instruction exception. The affected functionality is illegal-instruction detection in the decoder for register-register ALU operations. The trigger condition is any register-register ALU encoding with `instr[28] = 1`. The expected behavior is that the instruction is treated as illegal and the core raises an illegal-instruction trap before any subsequent instruction is executed.
